title: Salience vs. Polarity: a contrast-reduction experiment brief
purpose: A distinct counterpart to Iris's tonal-inversion experiment. Tests whether compositional salience (first-fixation on the doorway) tracks local contrast magnitude or structural position, by compressing the doorway brightness toward mid-gray without inverting global polarity. Provides a fixture image ID, arithmetic expectations, and a discriminating test design separating contrast-driven from structure-driven salience.
